+1 workaround verified on Windows 11 zh-CN.

Just implemented the `pwsh.cmd` wrapper from wqerrewetw's earlier comment in this thread:
```cmd
@echo off
chcp 65001 >nul
pwsh.exe %*
```
Set as `"shell": "C:/Users/leewe/.config/opencode/pwsh.cmd"` in `opencode.jsonc`.

**Before** (with `"shell": "pwsh.exe"`): Chinese filenames return garbled bytes like `�������ı���`
**After** (with `pwsh.cmd` wrapper): Same command returns `测试中文编码:你好世界 笔记材料 仓库库存` correctly

Also confirming fkyah3's analysis in this thread — the three-layer fix (chcp + `[Console]::OutputEncoding` + `$OutputEncoding`) is needed for full PowerShell coverage; the cmd.exe-only `chcp` prefix in his diff handles the non-PowerShell branch.

@Hona since fkyah3's fork isn't registered as an official fork (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/23636#issuecomment-4310183563), can you or another maintainer cherry-pick commit `be3d23604628975a6da7a4ade9fc0f03cb4ac8a5` into a feature branch and open the PR? 11 lines, 1 file, already validated on zh-CN and ru-RU. This would unblock zh/ja/ko/ru users who currently have to use either this `pwsh.cmd` wrapper or fork the repo.

AUTOMATED REVIEW: kiro auth plugin

**Security / malware: clean**
- `opencode-kiro@0.3.1` source matches npm tarball (gitHead 51fcc3ad)
- `kiro-acp-ai-provider@2.1.0` zero runtime deps, source matches npm (gitHead 365ec0389)
- No exfiltration, telemetry, eval, or obfuscation found
- Tool bridging via localhost HTTP IPC only (127.0.0.1, bearer-token protected)
- Filesystem: session cache in XDG_DATA_HOME, agent config `.kiro/agents/*.json`, tools in `/tmp/kiro-acp` – all expected

**Bundle size: negligible**
~137KB JS uncompressed total, no native deps

**Blocking issue: plugin runs unconditionally for all users**
`src/server.ts:server()` calls `notifyIfTokenExpired()` on every opencode startup, unconditionally. This `console.warn("Kiro is not logged in. Run 'kiro-cli login'…")` + TUI toast fires for EVERY user without kiro-cli installed, not just kiro-authed users.

Since this is bundled in `internalPlugins()`, all opencode users get spammed. Other bundled auth plugins (copilot, gitlab, poe, etc.) do not do this.

The plugin MUST be silent/disabled when the user has not authed to Kiro. Everything – including the startup warning, the sidebar config prompt, etc. – should only run for kiro-authed sessions.

Please gate all kiro-specific startup behavior behind an auth check, so non-kiro users see zero output / side effects.

Just a heads-up: a `cmd`-based wrapper may appear to work at first, but going through `cmd.exe` can introduce its own issues. In particular, parts of the command line, such as double quotes and other quoting/escaping-sensitive characters, may be consumed or reinterpreted by `cmd`, which can cause subtle bugs.

That is why I ended up writing a small Go-based wrapper instead.

There is also already an active PR for this: #31985. I used the code in that PR as a reference when implementing my Go wrapper locally, and it worked well in my environment.

I performed additional testing and can confirm this is not an API key or NVIDIA issue.

### Verified

* OpenCode: 1.17.11
* Provider: NVIDIA NIM
* Model: `nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b`

Using the **same API key**, **same endpoint**, and **same model**, NVIDIA's official Python example (OpenAI SDK) streams successfully.

Using the same API key in OpenCode, the model hangs indefinitely in the Build/Thinking phase.

Other NVIDIA NIM models continue to work correctly.

Since #24264 was caused by `options.extraBody` not being propagated for NVIDIA reasoning models, this may be a related regression or an additional compatibility issue specific to Nemotron 3 Ultra.

Additional debugging information:

I verified that this is not an authentication or NVIDIA API issue.

Using the **same NVIDIA API key**, **same endpoint** (`https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1`), and **same model** (`nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b`), NVIDIA's official Python example using the OpenAI SDK streams successfully and returns the expected response.

I then configured OpenCode to use the exact same API key via `/connect`. The model still hangs indefinitely in the Build/Thinking phase with no streamed tokens or error.

Other NVIDIA NIM models continue to work correctly in OpenCode.

This appears to be specific to OpenCode's handling of `nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b`, rather than an issue with the API key, endpoint, or NVIDIA service.

Since this issue has been linked to #24264 and #28385, it may indicate that Nemotron 3 Ultra requires additional handling beyond the previous `options.extraBody` propagation fix.

vscode's bug.

I reproduced this on OpenCode 1.17.11 with a long-running session. The DB tail showed automatic overflow compaction (`{"type":"compaction","auto":true,"overflow":true}`) followed by a compaction assistant failure (`MessageAbortedError`), and resuming the same session re-entered `agent=compaction mode=primary` instead of stopping on the original overflow.

I opened a small PR focused on that recovery gap: if overflow recovery summarization aborts/dies with a non-interrupt failure, treat compaction as failed and persist the original provider overflow as the assistant error. Real user/session interrupts are still preserved.

copilot opus can say it wants to use a tool without sending opencode an actual tool request. opencode then continues the session as if a tool request exists, and the next copilot request can fail with the assistant-prefill error.

The fix stops that loop. opencode now marks that turn as an error instead of asking copilot again. Normal tool use is unchanged, and the PR includes a regression test for this case.

# OpenCode GitHub Copilot Experimental Models Debug Report


## Issue Summary

OpenCode 1.17.11 does not automatically discover some GitHub Copilot Business / enterprise Experimental models that are visible to the same authenticated account when the request uses VS Code / Copilot CLI style headers.

The missing models are returned by the Copilot `/models` API only when these headers are included:

```http
Editor-Version: vscode/1.107.1
Editor-Plugin-Version: copilot-chat/0.26.7
Copilot-Integration-Id: copilot-developer-cli
```

With OpenCode's default model discovery headers, the models are absent. Manually registering the models in `opencode.json` and adding the same headers at the model level makes OpenCode able to use them.

## Environment

- OpenCode version: `1.17.11`
- OS: Linux
- GitHub Copilot auth in OpenCode: `oauth` configured for provider `github-copilot`
- Copilot plan/SKU: Copilot Business seat, login redacted
- OpenCode config path: `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`

## Reproduction Data

The same OpenCode GitHub Copilot OAuth token was used for both requests below. Only headers changed. Authorization values are redacted and not shown.

### Request A: OpenCode-style default headers

Request target:

```text
GET https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models
```

Headers used, excluding authorization:

```json
{
  "User-Agent": "opencode/1.17.11",
  "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2026-06-01",
  "Accept": "application/json"
}
```

Sanitized response summary:

```json
{
  "status": 200,
  "totalReturned": 33,
  "pickerEnabled": 16,
  "experimental": [],
  "allPickerIds": [
    "claude-haiku-4.5",
    "claude-opus-4.5",
    "claude-opus-4.6",
    "claude-opus-4.7",
    "claude-opus-4.8",
    "claude-sonnet-4.5",
    "claude-sonnet-4.6",
    "gemini-2.5-pro",
    "gemini-3-flash-preview",
    "gemini-3.1-pro-preview",
    "gemini-3.5-flash",
    "gpt-5-mini",
    "gpt-5.3-codex",
    "gpt-5.4",
    "gpt-5.4-mini",
    "gpt-5.5"
  ]
}
```

### Request B: VS Code / Copilot CLI-style headers

Request target:

```text
GET https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models
```

Headers used, excluding authorization:

```json
{
  "User-Agent": "GithubCopilot/1.155.0",
  "Editor-Version": "vscode/1.107.1",
  "Editor-Plugin-Version": "copilot-chat/0.26.7",
  "Copilot-Integration-Id": "copilot-developer-cli",
  "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2026-06-01",
  "Accept": "application/json"
}
```

Sanitized response summary:

```json
{
  "status": 200,
  "totalReturned": 39,
  "pickerEnabled": 21,
  "experimental": [
    "*/GLM/glm-5.1",
    "*/GLM/glm-5.2",
    "*/HUAWEI/glm-5.2",
    "*/QDeepseekV4/deepseek-v4-flash",
    "*/QDeepseekV4/deepseek-v4-pro",
    "*/Qwen37plus/qwen3.7-plus"
  ]
```

I read the code and tested on my machine. I can confirm some of the inconsistency described in this issue.

## Root Cause Analysis

### TUI: 
`pasteInputText()` calls `pastedFilepath()` to detect file paths from pasted text. When a valid path is found, it passes it to `readLocalAttachment()`, which reads the file content and embeds it as `[Image N]` / `[PDF N]`. The path string itself is consumed and never sent to the model.

### Desktop:
Pasting a plain text string like `C:\Users\...\image.png` into the Desktop app does **not** trigger attachment conversion — plain text is inserted normally (tested on Windows 10). The attachment behavior only occurs when an actual file is copied from the OS (the clipboard contains file items, not text). In that case, `handlePaste()` in `attachments.ts` detects `kind === "file"` items in `clipboardData.items` and converts them to attachments. 

## Why Ctrl+Shift+V Behavior Is Inconsistent

When running opencode in Windows Terminal with PowerShell, Ctrl+Shift+V still goes through bracketed paste, triggering file detection and consuming the path. On Linux, GNOME Terminal may intercept Ctrl+Shift+V and injects text as individual keystrokes, bypassing file detection. This is terminal-level behavior and unreliable across platforms.

## Proposed Approach

**TUI-only fix.** Add a new `Ctrl+Alt+V` keybinding (avoiding `Ctrl+Shift+V` due to inconsistent terminal interception) that pastes clipboard text without file path detection or content embedding. A new `prompt.paste-plain` command would read clipboard text and insert it directly via `input.insertText()`, bypassing `pastedFilepath()` / `readLocalAttachment()`.

The Desktop app is left for now — plain text path pasting works correctly there, and what users expect when copying actual files can be discussed separately.
